identity.title: Exploring the molecular chemistry and excitation in obscured luminous infrared galaxies. An ALMA mm-wave spectral scan of NGC 4418

paper_type_evidence.quote: We obtained an ALMA Cycle 0 spectral scan of the dusty LIRG NGC 4418, spanning a total of 70.7 GHz in bands 3, 6, and 7.

evidence.quote: Lying at $D$=34 Mpc, the galaxy is part of an interacting pair

question.value: What are the molecular abundances and excitation in the compact obscured nucleus of NGC 4418, and how do they compare with other Galactic and extragalactic environments?

evidence.quote: To obtain for the first time a multi-band spectral scan of a LIRG, in order to derive the molecular abundances and excitation, to be compared to other Galactic and extragalactic environments.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00820.S .

findings_qualitative.value: First extragalactic detection of HC3N (v7=1,v6=1) emission; spectrum dominated by vibrationally excited HC3N, HCN, HNC.

evidence.quote: The detection of emission from the (v7=1,v6=1) state of HC$_3$N is the first obtained in an extragalactic object.

claims.hypothesis: Does NGC 4418 contain a compact hot IR source?
claims.experiment: Vibrationally excited HC3N, HCN, HNC population analysis
claims.finding: Compact (<5 pc) optically thick IR source with Tb >350 K

evidence.quote: requires the presence of a deeply buried, optically thick source, of brightness temperature higher than 350 K

claims.hypothesis: Is NGC 4418's chemistry similar to Arp 220 and distinct from other environments?
claims.experiment: PCA of nine molecular abundances plus Tkin across 10 sources
claims.result: NGC 4418 and Arp 220 separated from others by PC3
claims.finding: A common peculiar chemistry typical of CONs

evidence.quote: We find that NGC 4418 and the ULIRG Arp 220 have similar molecular abundances and excitation, which set them apart from the other sources in the sample.

claims.hypothesis: Does molecular line emission contaminate the continuum?
claims.finding: Line contamination is serious for continuum studies in (U)LIRGs

evidence.quote: contamination by molecular emission, if not properly removed, could be a serious issue for studies of continuum emission

why_this_method.value: Source unresolved so spectrum extracted from visibilities instead of imaging

evidence.quote: Given the point-like nature of the emission, we chose not to image and clean the whole dataset

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Best power-law continuum fit overestimates 1 mm emission by >20%, so polynomial used instead

evidence.quote: The best power-law fit to the ALMA continuum points overestimates the emission at 1 mm by more than 20%

limitations_admitted.value: Unresolved emission: source size and common beam filling factor are the main uncertainties; line blending ~20%

evidence.quote: Because the emission is unresolved in the ALMA beam, the main uncertainty in our LTE/NLTE fit is the source size.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-beam, unresolved data; single assumed 0.4'' size and common filling factor for all species
Fixed 120 km/s line width and heavy blending make fits degenerate for many species
Comparison abundances from heterogeneous literature sources with different methods
Only 11 of 38 proposed tunings, so coverage is incomplete
